text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH

- Tansu Ciller's True Path Party has seen its number of parliamentary seats decrease from 135 after the last election in December 1995 to its present 115 seats, as MPs defect and resign from the party.
- Investment in the Isdemir steel plant in Iskenderun has ceased since it was announced it was to be privatised, posing threat to safety at the plant.
MILLIYET
- After an 18-year spell out of government, veteran left-wing party leader, Bulent Ecevit would be offered a cabinet place by prime minister-delegate, Mesut Yilmaz.
- The Capital Investment Board has finished preparing its indictment of Kombassan Holding, which is accused of supporting Islamist activitism.
HURRIYET
- Ciller's insistence on continuing in alliance with Islamist leader, Necmettin Erbakan, is leading to resignations from her party.
YENI YUZYIL
- Yilmaz will seek authority from senior fellow party members on Monday, before embarking on negotiations with other party leaers over forming a government.
- Preparatory work on the privatisation of Turk Telecom has been speeded up and should be finished by October.
RADIKAL
- Ciller's True Path Party is out of control, with few MPs, even those close to Ciller sharing her anger at Yilmaz and President Suleyman Demirel. More resignation from True Path are expected.
- Istanbul's Grand Bazaar is facing increasing competition from modern shopping centres and is threatened with being turned into a place solely for tourists.
CUMHURIYET
- The military dominated National Security Council, meeting on June 25 will look into the financial sources of Islamic activism.
ZAMAN
- Yilmaz is pinning all his hopes of forming a government on more resignations from Ciller's True Path Party. A senior True Path MP said there would be no more defections from his party.
- Pressure is mounting on Turkey to agree on a wordwide ban on landmines, which Ankara is resisting.
